tips.comment: No comment made

You’ve got to take Silver Knott seriously in the feature at Goodwood this afternoon but I think LIBERTY LANE will take all the beating at 2/1. SK has a 7lb penalty to overcome today after a success in the UAE earlier on in the year and I think that’ll make this task too tough for the gelding, meanwhile Expolanet has to overcome Sea The Stars’ 8% SR (A/E 0.36) over 10f at Goodwood. I struggled to make a case for the remainder so SK could just win by default as well as on merit; the son of Teofilo will be aided by a touch of moisture in the going and is dropping back into listed company after a fair 3.5l 3rd of 6 in the Huxley Stakes at Chester. C Lee brings a brilliant 48% SR (A/E 1.32) on favourites going right handed, owner Sheikh Mohammed Obaid Al Maktoum a 52% SR (A/E 1.38) with favs in 4yo+ races and K Burke does well with the latter's runners when he bred them (38% SR, A/E 1.29 when fancied).

Peace Nman is the Gosdens' only runner today. He has run well in the past, but on the evidence of his last run, a small each way is advised. If he is back to his best, he will go well and challenge, but it is an unknown.

MEYDAAN with thye benefit of a reappearance sharpener behind him can get involved. It has to be at least potentially significant that he returns to a track where he is a proven winner which counts for plenty at this venue and now possibly about to peak he appeals.

Reading through the racing press, you would think that Liberty Lane had this race all sewn up. My own opinion is that it is a very open-looking race with several runners having serious claims. My choice, Cash, should benefit from a tough seasonal opener at Sandown a month ago (6/8) and progress from that today in a slightly easier-looking race. He has a good draw, and the extra trip today ought to be of benefit.
Exoplanet remains completely unexposed here and can make a good impression on this field. Up against some smart horses, but could be better than them.
Has been inconsistent since last win at York last August, but it helps he has experience over C&D. Hoping the use of cheekpieces again and also drop down in class does the trick.

The selections career has been spent in Qatar. Has tackled 1m and 1m 4f with little joy but has won over 1m 2f and fairly consistent when racing over that distance. Unknown quantity but could surprise.

This could well be fought out between the top 2 in the market and 5/1 looks superb value for a stable that have brought horses over from Ireland to win this race twice in 4 years. Clearly that's a tip in itself and the horse took a massive leap forward when winning with something in hand on debut for the trainer last time out. Clearly the horse appears to have improved by a fair few pounds for the switch in stable and there could be much more to come now.

Santorini Star heads to Goodwood today after a commanding win at Brighton last month, where she stayed on strongly over 1m2f. She’s stepping up to 1m4f now, which should suit her running style. With a mark of 89 and a good draw, she’s got a solid shot at following up.

I've been keeping an eye on Orchard Keeper since her second to odds-on favorite on her second outing. She duly obliged just the once but has been the model of consistency with four places from five races since the win. Both trainer and jockey have been in good form lately, with Roger Varian having 5 wins and 5 places from the last 10 runners and Jack Mitchell riding 8 winners and 4 places from his last 30 rides.

Meribella is a horse who seems to go well after a break, so she could be near her best on her first run of the season. Top weights have a good chance at Goodwood over further than a mile due to the undulating and turning track, meaning the horses don't go at a strong gallop throughout the race. She is not the biggest but is very game.
Overture won 3 on the spin last season and can cause some problems for this field again here today. Looks to be underestimated in the betting and can be worth a bet here.
Bas Bleu won at the start of this month, and although up 4 lbs for that, the step up to C3 puts her well light amongst today's runners and worth a chance EW.
No comment made

Loving Look is a proven winner over middle distances, landing a mile and a quarter novice at Kempton and a mile and a quarter handicap at Newmarket last year. She returned with a respectable 3rd at Southwell over 1m and a quarter, showing us that she still retains ability, although she was behind Orchard Keeper, who took 2nd. Good EW claims here.

Gearing up for another crack at the Cesarewitch in October, but ran very well to finish 2nd at Southwell last month when running on nicely in the final stages. This is a drop in class and should make presence felt over this trip.

Mr Hampstead ran in the Derby last season. However, that was way beyond his ability, and he was duly tailed off. He has been gelded over the winter and returned over this course and distance recently, winning with a fair bit in hand. He was handed a seven-pound rise in the ratings after that success. However, I think this lightly raced runner can defy that hike and win again.

Only 3-29 but one of those wins did come over course and distance, albeit nearly 3 years ago. That was also the last time he tasted success but he's been slipping down the weights as a result and showed plenty of promise on reappearance when 4th off this mark at Chelmsford. Any kind of step forward will surely put him firmly in the mix this afternoon.

Almuhit heads to Goodwood today after a solid second in a big-field handicap hurdle at Punchestown last month. He’s back on the Flat now and has shown he stays well, with previous wins over similar trips. Off a mark of 84 and with conditions to suit, he’s got a fair chance if he brings his recent form across.
Trooper Bisdee was a prolific winner in the early part of last season and clearly can go well fresh so should not be inconvenienced by it being his first run and could go close in this contest.

TRITONIC hasn't been seen on the flat since last August and returns to this sphere reduced in the weights and down in grade as well. Now eight years old and hasn't found winning easy to come by, but maybe the drop in class is the tonic and he gets more competitive here. Hollie Doyle is another positive, and this price looks a few clicks higher than it should be.
They are returning this one back to the turf with an interesting jockey booking/change as they are dropping it down in class. A good value each way bet for the 4 places available.

Diamond Bay returned to action after a 165-day break to Goodwood three weeks ago, beating Sixpack by a nose. He has been upped another 4 lbs and is now being upped in trip. A chance is taken that he can follow up.

His barren run continues as it's now been nearly 2 years since the last win. However, still operating 5lbs higher than the last winning mark. Improvements required, which is helped by a drop down in class.

This well-bred gelding makes his debut for Gary Moore here, who won this race 3 years ago. The horse seems to fit the right age and ratings profile for this race, and the new trainer is arguably better at handling stayers than the previous trainer. The horse was sent off 10/3f last time out when fading a few furlongs out, but that could well have been down to the really bad ground. He races off the same mark here, and we are getting 16/1, so if you are prepared to write off that effort, then he looks very good value here.

I was very impressed with Fort George when he won at Newmarket recently. He was still showing inexperience but came through the field with a very smart turn of speed. He can only improve again, and I wouldn't be surprised to see him win this before heading for Royal Ascot.

Stayed on nicely to finish runner-up to an impressive winner last time. Gone up a couple of pounds, but that may be lenient considering the third has since won very well, franking the form. There should be more to come from this prominent racer. It is just a shame he is drawn widest of all; otherwise, this would have been a bigger bet.

Take an EW chance on 3yo irish gelding Sky Advocate here. His two turf runs ended in a 3rd and 4th in quite big fields. Makes his hc debut here off a fair mark and the booking of amazing Rossa Ryan catches the eye. Holds every chance to be in the mix here.
Disappointed on reappearance last time, his first run for Balding, having previously been with Stoute. Worth persevering with and has an each-way chance.

Beat a subsequent Listed 2nd on debut who hasn’t had the form franked by Alpine Trail, but it still suggests a mark of 86 could be generous enough for this horse in handicap company for the first time. Whilst he might not have the highest ceiling of these, he just looked the one that was handicapped to do better at this stage on the form evidence, and there isn’t much more to it. He will hopefully get a nice tow into it from one of the outsiders drawn alongside, and with the favorite on his other side, hopefully he’s around the action late on.

The 3yo filly has 1 win from 4. Decent return run last month, after 6 months off the track, which was an AW debut. She should be better for the run, drop in grade, and will be happier back on grass. She was a close second in a novice stakes last Oct., giving 7lb to both the 3rd and 4th. Those two have run well since. Her mark looks handy in this handicap.

A couple of back-to-back All Weather wins have pushed us up the weights here, but we are back in a class 4 instead of a class 2, which we were in last time. We bombed in that, coming in 8th of 8. Can we be competitive off this mark?

First run for new stable of Gary and Josh Moore (SR 15%) having moved from Alice Haynes' yard. Lengthy absence of almost a year to overcome. Two-year-old form is decent. Won a Class 5 maiden and all three other efforts were respectable in Class 2 company. Up in trip now but, by Coulsty, pedigree suggests he's a good chance of staying the trip. Lowest handicap mark of these in what looks a decent Class 4 0-85 contest for 3yos.
Top speed rating. 2 from 2 on good ground and strong market confidence. Several rivals are exposed here and none have posted a rating close to this horse in the last year
Havana Pusey won last time out after a duff start but kept on well on the run-in to take the front from 1f out. This makes me think today's step up to 7f could suit.

Diamondonthehill is a consistent and dependable type who gained a deserved first win of the year in a 7 runner handicap at Lingfield over 7f on the AW track 25 days ago. Only 2 lb higher for that success, which seems fair given the manner of the win. Remains in good heart and should be firmly in the win mix once again, especially if getting a decent pace to aim at.

4yo gelding Mafnood was a good 3rd of 10 on first run for new trainer George Baker and on seasonal debut after a 215 day break. Should show further improvement and this step back to 1m could suit really well. Stable and jockey in great form, so should be in the mix here.

Mister Bluebird resumed with a very good run on seasonal debut, which puts this CD winner in the frame here for trainer Heather Main. Operating just below its last winning mark, it has a chance under Jack Mity.

Epsom winner last season who returned with a good effort when only just denied at Kempton last month. Well beaten at Ascot last time but will appreciate step up to 7 furlongs and is just 1lb above last winning mark so should run well.

CAPOTE'S DREAM probably wouldn't be the outsider of this lot. The mark looks workable based on runs on the flat at Newbury and Doncaster at the end of last year. The stable tends to do better than usual here, and there are others that I can pick more holes in. Might be a stretch for the win, but there are each-way claims, and he could hit the jackpot.
No comment made

This horse's CD 3rd in September was won in a finale blistering time. Whilst 6th from 7 on seasonal reappearance, he was far from disgraced. Just a lb above his last winning mark at Newmarket, he could be ready to go in with a return here and that run in his legs. Winning almost a year to the day at Windsor made it 2 wins from 4 runs in May, so he could be one to catch now off the back of that recent effort where he was just a touch too keen and fresh. If he can run anywhere near his best (peak RPR of 94, 5 starts back), then he can go in off a mark of 83. Rossa Ryan is 1/1 on him and takes the ride here.

Enchanting loves it here at Goodwood with two wins and two places from her four runs here. Didn't show up in her last race and the trainer couldn't explain why, so hopefully just a blip. But she won her penultimate race, which happened to be here, and has had time to recover since. She has won once after a short break. Always runs over this distance and has form on all goings from Good to Heavy. Hollie Doyle in the plate for all of her races bar one, and even then finished 2nd of 4 here.
With 4 wins and 9 places from 29, Moulin Bouj is a tough cookie, especially on turf. I think this fast 5f dash will suit him to the ground. E.W. in the hope his odds drift.

A consistent 4-year-old filly, she is a course and distance winner who has finished in the first three 11 times from 21 starts on turf and who was last seen finishing 3rd of 8 over 5 furlongs at Bath in April. Mason Paetel takes over on board today and claims 7 lbs. Distance and good going suit.

Alcazan has won twice over 6 furlongs here at Goodwood, with the last coming in August last year off a mark of 72. She did win at Ascot over 5 furlongs last year. Having dropped back to her last winning mark and with Joe Leavy taking off an extra 3 lbs, she looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

No show @ Epsom Lto, but that is a very unique track and a lot of horses do not take to it. Was in very good form on the Aw prior to that run, but is a C/D winner so return to this surface and course not an issue. Retains a decent mark of 86 here, good jockey up and very shrewd trainer who does very well in the sprinting sphere, best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons, making current 11/1 very good Ew value in the race.

Michaela's Boy has slipped to an attractive mark and looked in need of the run on return to action earlier this month. The nap ran well when 3rd here last summer and will have every assistance in the saddle with Rossa Ryan booked to ride.

First run of the season and first time after a wind op could mean that today's not the day for this speedball, but he has been here on 3 occasions and showed up well. This fast 5f is right up his street and he could be a real each way player.

A fair to middling sort of a run last time under Hollie Doyle was anything but eye-catching. It should be noted, though, that we are on a previous winning mark, and maybe the 7lb jockey claim could help us here.
Has a great turn of foot, usually from the front end, but even came from behind to win before. Has to be a solid each-way chance here at a good price too.
Still looks to be on a good mark, and if we excuse the run at the tricky Epsom course, has been in decent nick. Won back in February, and although this race looks competitive, has each-way chances.
Only beaten a neck over C&D last time out in a similar contest. He is down a pound and has a 5lb claimer to take off a bit of his burden and he is 2/7 with a second for this stable so far.

6yo gelding Fishermans Cottage is in nice form winning his penultimate race and would have gone much closer lto if he wouldn't have met a lot of traffic. Goes well on fast ground and should be in the mix here.

SAVALAS is crying out for a step up to six or seven furlongs but connections still race him over five and a half furlongs. He is a dual course and distance who seems to put his best efforts in when racing in double figured fields. Eleven runners today with a good low draw.
Has never won on turf but with such a low mark on this surface I think it's worth a go.

Still unclear if he is better suited to turf. However, LTO effort was poor when only 11 of 11 at Wolverhampton. So, switch to turf might be beneficial, especially with dropped mark and also has experience over C&D.
Cindy Lou Who changed yards for the return at the start of the month. Although seventh, she was still not far away after not getting a clear run. I would expect more now, second up and 2 lbs lighter.

He looks to be on a handy mark and really should make good use of it. The top of the card looks far too short-priced for any value considering the ability of the runners. Off the bench could score today in this low-key affair.
Twice course winner (one over C&D), Mrembo has shown a return to form with two close finishes in her last two races. Drops a grade for this and should go close.

3 C/D wins and now drops to 1 lb below the first of those wins back in 2023. Good 3rd LTO against a horse who has since completed a 4-timer (Beauld as Brass). Jockey booking tells me they mean business today. WIN BET.

Dappled Light heads to Bath today after a commanding win at Chepstow just ten days ago, where he surged clear to score by three lengths. He carries a 5lb penalty but still looks well-treated off a mark of 59.
Going against the favorite is always risky at Bath. Solid EW proposition. Best C&D and speed rating in the field.

Done well since joining Daniel and Claire Kubler, picking up a couple of wins at Brighton last season. Good efforts on the all-weather in a couple of starts this spring before a poor effort last time, but has slipped down to just 1 lb above last winning mark now. So, it would be no surprise to see him bounce back this afternoon.

Claxton Bay heads to Bath today after a couple of solid runs on the all-weather earlier this year. He’s back down to Class 6 and off a mark of 61, which is within his winning range. With a decent draw and conditions to suit, he could bounce back to form if he finds his rhythm.

Gained 5th career win when successful over an extended mile at Wolverhampton in February. Solid run when placed over this course and distance on penultimate start. Slightly disappointing at Doncaster last time but now down a pound and capable of going close.

WESTON COURT probably needed the run last time out as it was the first trip in 245 days. Entitled to come on from that and could get involved from the last winning mark. Handily drawn as well, so with going, grade, and conditions all suitable, it's very difficult to rule out too readily. May need another run to gain more sharpness but worth a look at this price.

Has two Southwell and a Chelmsford win to his name, and they may have found a turf race in which he could spring a surprise. Five-pound jockey claim will be useful in a tight handicap. Dropped four pounds and now four pounds below the last winning mark. Although only fifth at Lingfield last time, he wasn't beaten that far and looks too big a price in this race.

A 3-year-old filly from powerhouse trainer W J Haggas, ridden by A J Farragher. Lightly raced but with immense potential. She’s bred for stamina and speed, and connections suggest confidence. Dominant in debut performance, she’s expected to handle this step up well.

With just the three runners, this may not be the test that Bosphorus Rose needs. Uptown Girl is yet to show a return on her owner's £105,000 investment but might have an easier opportunity than last time at Ascot in a stronger race.

The only one in this race with run experience. Just missed out by a neck on victory then at Ascot by acting amateurish inside the last 100 yards. So perhaps now, with the 1 furlong increase in trip, may capitalize second time of asking.

TAHALEL is a well-bred, unraced two-year-old filly by Blue Point. The dam is unraced. The course, distance, and going should suit her. She should run well on her racecourse debut and could well be able to win this race.
The yard have hit form so I'm having a small wager on this well bred newcomer. Anything can happen in these races but there has been some support for her already, which is a good omen.
Tsuki was impressive when winning a Class 4 maiden at Goodwood on debut 3 weeks ago. She will have learned a lot from that and can go in again.

A well-bred debutant from the Charlie Appleby yard, Wild Desert looks primed for a strong run. With top jockey Billy Loughnane aboard and favourable odds of 2.10, he’s expected to perform well under first-time conditions, showcasing potential class and solid yard form.

3yo irish filly Adorla Of Achill was a good 4th of 12 lto over the extended mile at Nottingham. This was her first run as a 3yo and on turf. So could easily make another step forward here today and should be in the mix.

Glenridding heads to Haydock today after a couple of solid runs this season, including a third at Lingfield in March. He’s back down to a mark of 69, which is 3lb lower than his last winning rating, and the return to turf could suit. If he gets a clean trip, he’s got a decent shot at getting involved.

This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today as they are returning it back to the turf with an interesting jockey booking/change. This is his only ride of the day, also dropping down in trip slightly.

Groundsman lines up in the Oakmere Homes Supporting Macmillan Grassroots Handicap (Class 5) over 1 mile, with £4,500 to the winner. Trained by Richard Fahey, one of the leading yards in the north, the stable has had a slow start to the season but has produced three winners in the last fortnight, suggesting momentum is building. Groundsman ran four times as a juvenile, showing promise in his first three starts before undergoing a gelding operation. He was well-backed at Chester, delivering an impressive third-place finish on 21st September. He was declared for Doncaster in April, but the ground was too quick, leading connections to wait for softer conditions. Now, with Danny Tudhope booked, and expected good ground at Haydock, he should be primed for a strong seasonal return. His handicap mark of 68 looks manageable, and with conditions finally in his favour, he appears well-placed for success.

I am not sure that the going had anything to do with his last run, even though last year's win and other decent runs were on softer going. He has still done well on a quicker surface, and LTO was probably a case of needing the run. The stable has been going well, and I'm expecting a better effort today.
Finished very strongly last time and just failed to get up. The winner failed by the narrowest of margins to follow up next time, so form looks reliable.
Went down narrowly at Wolverhampton in October and has been placed the last twice. A pound higher now but looks to have been well placed here.
Beaten just a neck last time and put up a bit for that. We are back on turf here and hopeful. We did come third previously off this mark, and we are carrying the same jockey as last time.

Three winners, a 3rd, and an unplaced last three racing days for the stable. Zizi looks a promising type. 1m1f winner as a 2yo, so 1m2f today is probably as short as she would want. Although 6th of nine at Wolverhampton, she was only 3 lengths off the leader and never involved.

Carrying a 7Lb penalty for very comfortable 5.25L win here over CD on last run without coming off the bridle . This is a tougher looking race but perfectly capable of back to back wins for Team Skelton .
Edna E Mode was a decent 2nd last time out at Ludlow under Jonathan Burke. Now in the hands of Ciaran Gethings. Finishing in front of Manala that day. She should go well at a very generous 10/1.

LA CANTATE is likely up to running from an opening handicap mark of 89. She is a four year old filly with an all-French pedigree possibly therefore with maturity beyond her years and she comes from a shrewd yard who know how to lay one out to land bets. Every indication from her family this step up in distance will suit on her first run in this sphere , so the market can help us.
Barranco seems likely to follow up his win under a penalty after winning at Bangor with authority on 17th May. In good hands and should follow up.

Jac Jumper, 6yo, yet to win a chase but has been 2nd 4/8 times (two here over 2m4f good). In several of his last races, all over further than today, he has appeared to be just a tad short on stamina to see him home over that trip. The drop to 2m today can pay dividends as he gets the course well and will enjoy the ground.
2nd time over the fences, having been pulled on debut fence run. Runs on good ground, now lowly weighted. Trainer and jockey fare well at this course.

JIMMYJEROO represents a bang-in-form trainer and has plenty of confidence coming from the saddle with Brendan Powell among the winners. He has the cheek pieces fitted often a sign of intent and in good shape himself at present he looks a value play in. thos small field.

Despite being the outsider of the field, this one looks great value to me. He's two pounds higher than his last winning mark, but more importantly than that is the fact that his yard is in such good form. He's had a pipe opener over hurdles and now back over the bigger obstacles, he can go very close.

Sits just 3 lbs above his last winning mark. Dropping down in grade this time.
Both chase wins come in this grade. One of his chase wins came over CD. He absolutely bolted up on that occasion, beating A Definite Getaway by 15L. A very dominant, easy success. That form looks better now with the runner-up winning 3 of his 7 runs since.
He's not managed to get his head in front since, but has placed off a 7 lbs higher mark than this twice, bumping into well-handicapped horses on each occasion.
He showed promise on his penultimate run, finishing 3rd in a class 2 race at Fontwell. Although he has had a lesser run since. if he can get back to that CD form, he's probably the one to beat in this type of race.

The Warren Greatrex-trained Sageburg County is only 2 lbs above his last winning mark. That win was on this ground, over a similar trip in Class 3 company. This Class 4 handicap looks well within his capabilities, and with conditions in his favor, if he runs to his mark, he could prove hard to beat.
Point winner with seven defeats over hurdles. But with this weaker maiden and longer distance, it has to be worth exploring, especially with Sean Bowen at the helm.
Jomig Des Bois's consistent Bangor performance highlights potential; latest handicap effort is solid. Sets standard here and should be competitive in this company.

The model I run suggests Money To Burn can win this one. This result has been driven by Money To Burn having a reasonable RPR compared to the rest of the field. All horses go out carrying the same weight, and the trainer has a high RTF%. The model has issued a 'very low' rating, suggesting a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Slade Shore can win this race. This result has been driven by Slade Shore having the highest RPR of the runners here without being penalised for it in the weights. Slade Shore last ran 10 days ago and looks to build on a 5th place finish after needing the run after a break. The model has issued a 'high' staking indicator, which translates to a 2pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
High Fibre has finished placed 3 times over hurdles. Faces a drop in class here and looks a cut above the opposition in this race.

The model I run suggests Regal Cavalier can win this race. Regal Cavalier lines up here with the second highest RPR of this 9-runner race. It is one of the younger horses here and is looking for progression over this 2m maiden hurdle. Placed well with a good second 30 days ago and looks to go one better. The model has indicated a 'low' reading, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Outran odds of 50/1 when making hurdles debut at Worcester over two miles but wasn’t given a hard time. Has the scope to improve on that and holds decent claims.
Native Moon's great Ascot victory showcased ability. A 5lb rise is manageable. Displays promise and is open to further progression in this contest.
12-year-old who cashed in on a reduced mark at Carlisle last month and followed that up with a win at Warwick 18 days ago. Up 6 lb but is a great contender. Great each-way shout.

The model I run suggests Taritino can win this race. This result has been driven by Taritino having the second highest RPR of the 10 runners in this field, but a reasonably low official ranking. Placed recently, so comes here in decent form. Is a previous distance winner and Sam Twiston Davies picks up the reins for this 2m trip.

A chance is taken here each way with Battle of Omdurman who drops in grade again here. Won when fresh on hurdles debut after leaving Ollie Sangster so at 9/1 each way we put down our cash....and hope!

Rated 82 on the flat which equates to 117 over hurdles, but is currently on a mark of 93, so is definitely under performing so far with no wins from 11, but has come close over CD with a 2nd and an eye-catching 3rd last time out, so time to shine now and looks nailed on to at least finish in the frame. The 13/2 looks rather generous to me.

Looks like they ended last season by just trying to get him lower in the handicap, which certainly worked.
The seven-year-old is now 13lb below his last winning mark and these types are always interesting on the back of breaks. I would have liked to see cheekpieces back on, but certainly not one I would want to be pricing this big.

Made All failed to win in his first 16 starts, but the step up to 1m4f and change of stable brought a big improvement when he won at Catterick last week. He has a 5lb penalty here but looks to have a good chance of following up.
Stayed on nicely to win at Carlisle last time out and connections of AGATHON send him out quickly in a bid to potentially make hay whilst this one seems to be in form.
With form figures of 1, 5, 2, 1, 1 on the all-weather coming into this contest, we are, of course, hoping that we are on such a roll that the weight increase won't stop us.

Lady Phoebe steps into the 19:47 PMW Quarries Handicap (Class 6) at Pontefract, a 1m4f5y contest on good to firm ground. Trained by Adam Nicol, this 4-year-old filly carries a rating of 45 into this 8-runner field. 
In her most recent outing on May 12 at Catterick, Lady Phoebe finished a respectable fourth over 1m4f, beaten by 5 lengths on good to firm ground. This performance suggests she's maintaining her form and can be competitive in this field. 
With the going at Pontefract expected to be good to firm, conditions should suit Lady Phoebe well. Her experience over the distance and recent form make her an appealing each-way proposition at likely generous odds.

Two runs this year for the lightly raced 4-year-old after coming off a 6-month break. He was 2nd of 12 three weeks ago, over this 12f trip and on quick ground. No chance behind the smart winner, but the selection and the 3rd had pulled 5L clear of the rest. Same mark for this contest, room for improvement, and he might be underestimated.

Has improved since being gelded and being sent handicapping, showing his best form when third at Beverley last time out. Kept plugging away that day so should appreciate this track and looks the type who has better to come.
Vibrant Pearl finished 2nd on debut over 6f and will be suited by this drop to the minimum trip. The winner that day looked useful so that could represent a decent level of form.
This track suits this mare. The form of her 2nd has been franked even though this is a step up in class. Should go well.
See Winter Crown comments. Competitive 5F race. Rally is in form but races off 65 and is 3 lbs higher than his last winning mark.
Kept on well when winning over 6 furlongs on the Wolverhampton tapeta last time out and should be suited by the uphill finish here dropping in trip.
Like both this horse and Protest Rally in this race, having seen both run live. On balance, better value with Winter Crown due to speed rating and a career-low mark. Should bounce back.
Last win back in 2022 and has not been too active recently, but also has experience over C&D and is still running off the last winning mark. Needs to make improvements to have any chance tomorrow.

A beaten favorite over a mile at Thirsk 6 days ago, but can bounce back on the strength of the previous run on penultimate start when beaten a head over the same track and trip by subsequent winner, Visibility, who boosted the form yesterday when winning at Yarmouth.
Not the clearest of runs last time, but we have come a close 2nd off this mark. Obviously, a repeat of that should see us go close here.

Captain Corelli ended last term in September, after winning four in a row, with the last win in C4 being by nearly 4L. It's worth a shot that the yard has him ready for this return to C5 to continue his progress.

Five-year-old Zoffany mare has won three of 19 starts on turf and, while out of form, returned with an outing over seven furlongs at Doncaster less than a month ago and is entitled to come on for that run. Billy Garritty rides for Mick and David Easterby. First-time visor tried. Low handicap mark of 57 (lowest weight in the race), eight pounds below last winning mark. Always been a bit in and out form-wise, and on good racing ground could get involved.

Farough has to be opposed here given Sheikh Abdullah Almalek Alsabah’s 13% SR (A/E 0.38) with favs who ran 15 to 28 days ago plus R Varian’s 21% SR (A/E 0.47) with market leaders at Pontefract. Next up UBETTERSEETHIS makes the most appeal against given his two runs previously; the son of Ubettabelieveit was denied by a head on debut here at Ponte over 5f last month before being upped in class at Beverley and being a comfortably beaten odds-on favourite. He was hampered early on that day but I see S James as a jockey upgrade from 3lb claimer W Pyle and C Lidster’s 39% SR (A/E 1.69) with fancied runners on good to firm adds further confidence. 5/2 taken.

Ryan Moore is booked for his only ride of the day. He was successful on the selection in a maiden 2 starts ago. He then ran with credit in his final 2-year-old start 223 days ago at Newmarket, and the AOB yard have won 7 of the last 12 renewals.
Deserves this step up in class, tackling Group company for the first time, after destroying a field of maidens by 5L LTO. Will have the fitness edge over some of these, so is worth a bet.
3rd in the Ballysax, sandwiched in-between black type winning horses. Time for this Night of Thunder colt to win a black type. Dropping back to his winning maiden trip may just do the trick.

Shackleton has the best form but all of his rivals have the benefit of a recent run. His stablemate Thrice ran as if needing his seasonal debut at Chester but has some decent form in the book and should strip fitter today.

Keke is a 5-year-old gelding trained by sprint specialist Edward Lynam. He is a talented horse with 5 wins out of 13 starts. He is a two-time course winner, once over CD, and is ground versatile. He posted a career-high RPR of 101 and runs off 92 today, so he is feasibly well treated. He finished 4th out of 25 in the Bold Lad Sprint over CD just three starts back, beaten just 1.75 lengths. He handles big fields and seems to thrive at the Curragh. He is my short-priced banker of the day under W J Lee.

I’m willing to take a tentative poke here with Johnny Murtagh’s 5yr old gelding DAAMBERDIPLOMAT, who drops significantly in class after contesting a competitive Class 2 all-weather sprint (6f) at Newcastle 35 days ago (beaten 4¾ lengths).
This son of COTAI GLORY has just one turf win to his name but hasn’t run badly at the Curragh - most notably finishing 4th on his last visit, just a head behind today’s rival COLLECTIVE POWER. Jockey Ben Coen returns to the saddle, having partnered DAAMBERDIPLOMAT to 2 of his 4 career wins. Coen is in solid form, with a 31.82% place strike rate over the past month and 23.92% here at the Curragh across five years. Even more encouraging is his 40.45% place strike rate for Murtagh in the past year - part of 8 recent wins for the yard in the past 30 days.
So, why tentative? It’s no secret this charge prefers the all-weather, and the possible forecasted rain could compromise his chances - though one would assume the trainer would withdraw him if the ground goes against him.
Still, at 20/1, 5 places and a big class drop, I’m happy to have a little skin in the game.

Collective Power is worth a play at odds of 12-1. Low in this handicap running off a mark of 82 and Sorcha Woods claims an apprentice's 7lbs allowance. Ted Lynam brings a strong string to the Curragh this afternoon. Second and then first for this jockey on final two AW starts at Dundalk before running decently at Naas last time out. Struggled with traffic problems there, doing his best work late on. Seven years of age with a career tally of 8 wins from 64 runs.

LITTLE QUEENIE is treated well by being eased a further 4lb in the handicap. That is on the back of her reappoearance effort and she should strip fitter for that effort. With potential now to be seen to good effect second run back she appeals as a value each-way play.

Decent effort at Cork last time, his first start for 9 months, when a close up 5th over 7f. Travelled well during the race but failed to get a clear run at a critical stage so did well to finish as close as he did. Decent place claims.

Five career wins include three over today's course and distance. Found things happening too fast dropped to five furlongs for his seasonal return, but will have come on for that first outing in well over five months. He has to be in the mix racing over a track and trip that clearly suits.

TANGO FLARE gets an experienced jockey booked looking favourably treated for his reappearance. He has shown winning form when returning for a new season and he comes from a yard who now how to get one ready for a punt in handicap company under both codes.
Low draw, tough mark remark the Racing Post, but with form figures of 3, 2, 2, 1, 5, albeit on the all-weather, we shouldn't be quite written off just yet.

Looks a good thing here. Stable in red-hot form. 50% strike rate in May, 10 winners from 20 runners. Selection was not knocked about on debut last time, having been caught further back than ideal and will come on for the run and improve.

Glory To Be makes its debut at 3yo instead of 2yo and I can see why. Yard will quickly move on from this to bigger things. When looking into it's pedigree the 2yo form isn't good. When looking at parents 3yo form the difference is incredible c2 c1 group races plenty of prize money. This is the angle this shrewd yard will be aiming at after this. 20/1 e/w nap.

Team Twomey are in sparkling form, and their entry is predictably a short-priced favourite. But debutant Charasson could well make a race of it. The Kodiac filly is extremely well-related and with a yard who are also in fine form.

Thrice raced daughter of No Nay Never & Lucky At The Bay ( Dam's sire Lucky Pulpit ) who makes her seasonal reappearance run here after a 203 day break likely to be much better built and more professional over on the business end now as a 3yo D Dias's inmate is likely to progress well this term and is open to plenty of improvement especially now as a 3yo steps up in trip tackling the full 6 furlong trip for the first time that most certainly being a good move by her connections as this new trip can help bring out that improvement jockey G M Ryan takes the ride and can give Never Not Lucky the perfect ride here at the Curragh expect this good looking chestnut to be a whole different proposition
Noble Name fought back well at Tipperary when 3rd in a mares' bumper following her win in a point, and there is a good chance that she can outbattle Better Times and Cinnamon Roll in this bumper.
Clearly struggling to get 3 miles in PTP races, but he's not badly bred and with a top yard, so can perhaps be seen to better effect now trying a bumper.

Ontheropes takes a drop in class for this long-distance hunter's chase. He has a very good past record, which included 5th in last year's Scottish Grand National. Although his only point win was this January, his only chase win was back in October 2021.

GRANGE SOLIDIER could be worth chancing sent out under rules at a similar time last year which resulted in a win. He showed signs when pointing latest that he may be about to come back to hand , so potentially a spring developer he appeals.

Ocean Manifest is a 4-year-old making a stable debut for Stephen Thorne, a trainer in great form, winning with his last three runners. If reproducing his debut run at Fairyhouse last year, when he finished 3/16 behind Four Blondes under Seammie Heffernan, posting aa RPR of 83, the 3/16 Monasterboice won the next three races. The 4/16 Leaders Listen won on the next start, and the 5/16 Artful Approach also won on the next start. He has an absence to overcome, but with the yard in such good form, Ocean Manifest has to be considered off a lowly mark of 71 with Jack Kearney's 3lb apprentice claim.
Won over a mile last time out. Interesting to see Colin Keane hang around to assist as Port Louis attempts to defy a 4lb hike and may well be able to do so back at his optimum trip.

Now 4 pounds lower today. Showhound had been in solid form earlier in the year, including a win at Newcastle in January, and wasn’t disgraced when mid-division in a massive 25 runner handicap here last time, where he was only 7 lengths off the winner despite being below his best. The return of cheekpieces could sharpen him up, and he's got a more manageable race this time. Definite player if back to his earlier form.

A Friday night barnburner at the Curragh - what’s not to like? A wide-open 23-runner mile handicap, and while we’re not quite in “close your eyes and throw a dart” territory, it’s still fiercely competitive. That said, I’m sticking with Chris Timmons’ 4-year-old filly AUBURN AVENUE, who I tipped here 18 days ago (7f, Good).
She didn’t get the smoothest of passages that day - checked a couple of times - but stayed on well to finish fifth, showing a willing attitude. This daughter of PHOENIX OF SPAIN has been dropped 3lbs for that effort and now gets a significant jockey upgrade. Chris Hayes takes over in the saddle and arrives here in fine form, with a 35.29% place strike rate over the past month and a strong 25.41% place rate at the Curragh over the past five years.
There is a slight concern if the forecast early evening showers affect the going, but she didn’t disgrace herself on heavy going at Leopardstown (9f) last October. Now stepping up in trip, racing off a 13lb lower mark than her last Curragh outing in stronger company, and with a top rider booked, I’ll stay loyal and give this girl another chance.

This went in my tracker some years ago, and I might have mentioned it before in my write-ups that I thought Cordouan had some talent but seemed to get distracted and that some form of headgear would help. Well, it did finally happen last August, and it won. It has now changed hands, and the headgear has gone (I believe). I didn't bet on either race this year but did get place money (Skybet) in the first race, which I thought was a stretch first up over 1m 2f and was a decent 5th last time out back down to today's trip of 1m. It had a slow start, so filled in at the rear and then had some traffic problems, so pretty good really. 2lb down, and the headgear looks a thing of the past.

Shigar looks interesting at a big price in the concluding handicap. He has won 3 times on the flat, with two coming in Britain. He was placed 4 times last season before winning a Navan handicap off a mark of 80. He has been unplaced in two races off 84 since, the last being on seasonal debut at Cork earlier this month. He has, though, been dropped to 81, and Jamie Orr claims 10 lbs. He looks a good each-way bet with 6 places on offer.

BUCKLES AND BOLTS could fare much better with the headgear removed down in trip today. He is one of multiple entries for a shrewd Irish yard in Sheila Lavery and with an in-form claming apprentice jockey aboard this potential improver from his reduced mark could surprise.

Not an obvious choice but wasn't beaten far on handicap debut at Leopardstown last month, and subsequently had no luck in running over seven furlongs here earlier this month. Came up against some much higher rated opponents at Killarney latest, and certainly far from disgraced on his first attempt at a mile. Can go well returning to handicap company.

Looked potentially smart when winning his bumper just over a year ago. Plenty of decent horses have come out of that race subsequently. Has since had 2 runs over hurdles, including on reappearance last time when runner-up. Will appreciate the step up in trip today and is the one to beat.

Hills Of Glory was just pipped at the post at Naas in December over this distance in what was to date the closest call in search of the maiden win. It is that showing which provides the basis for siding with here at a similar price.
Jazz De Cotte has some decent form but is giving weight away to all but one rival. Perhaps his stablemate, Welcome Back, can get his jumping together and begin to realize his undoubted potential.

ECO PETE won a bumper race at this course in December 2021. His last two races have been over fences, but prior to that, he ran here over 22f. That race was last August where he finished 6th of 7 behind Intense Approach. Dropped in trip today, he may be able to gain a first hurdle win on his 11th attempt. He has previously finished placed three times. His official rating of 102 gives him a chance of getting involved.

The model I run suggests ParkGarve can win this race. ParkGarve lines up here with a relatively high RPR, but goes out carrying a relatively low weight when comparing to the other 15 runners in this race. ParkGarve is the only horse here who has placed or run any kind of form recently, coming third 10 days ago. The model has indicated a 'very low' stake reading, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is largely as a result of the small gap in predicted positioning to second place.

MIRACLE BEAUTY has the benefit of being drawn high here. She won her maiden at Naas in October and was a beaten favourite last time out when having her first run in a handicap at Naas over 6f. She wears first time cheekpieces here. Sure to go well.

Staysound Susie won twice last season and is now back down to that last winning mark. She was beaten just 0.5 lengths at Naas 11 days ago and down 2 lbs. Looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

Completely destroyed her field on penultimate start at Dundalk. Not quite in the same form last time under 8 lb extra, and the handicapper has given her a couple of pounds respite, so she must have a chance.
The experienced Greek Flower is a consistent sort who often goes well fresh and she might be able to defy top weight here with Jamie Powell taking off 3lb.

Island Girl makes plenty of appeal at a double figure price in an open looking race at the Curragh today. The filly ran a promising third last time out and looks primed to win soon with luck in running.

A winner at 6f on yielding ground, well beaten behind East Hampton on reappearance at Naas over 7f soft to yielding in March. Has had 2 months off, probably waiting for better going as the yard is in excellent form. Trying cheekpieces for the first time, should be in the mix. NAP.

She’s entered off a mark of 81 in what looks a wide-open contest, and with good to firm ground forecast, conditions should be ideal. Adrian Murray has placed her well here, and this step back up in trip combined with the big-field scenario should allow her to settle early and finish late, which looks to be her preferred running style.
While she’ll need to step forward from what she’s shown so far, I think there’s more to come, and she looks overpriced at current odds. She’s one of those lightly raced types that could pop up in a race like this, especially with a strong pace to aim at.

ROSATO is an interesting filly arriving fresh at the foot of the weights for a shrewd yard. From her still modest mark she woud of course be eligible for weaker handicaps than she faces here , but now a four year old she may have developed well in her time spent on the sidelines and she has an often favoured high draw over this straight six furlongs.

Sights Unseen keeps knocking on the door but finding one too good, and I wouldn't fancy him if it comes to a battle with the experienced campaigner True Destiny, who ran his usual wholehearted race last time out and can register a 9th career success tonight.

SIR CARNEGIE ran well on his penultimate start suggesting he had a race of this nature in him. He has a sound sire for races in Ireland under the NH code and he remains a five year old capable of progress from his lowly hurdles mark.

We are coming from maiden hurdles, point-to-points, and non-handicap chases here, into a handicap hurdle. It's difficult to weigh up our chances in many ways, but it could equally be good as it could be bad. 3rd LTO in a point.

Ran to a fairly useful level in a light two year old campaign, just the three starts, putting up her best performance when a close 2nd at Leopardstown over a mile on her second start. Not been seen since the end of September and with this trip likely to be on the short side given her entry in the Irish Oaks although this doesn’t look a particularly strong maiden.
Well-bred Juddmonte filly who is realistically placed on her belated debut. Disappointing if she can't at least make the frame for top connections.
COLLECTING COIN, third on his racecourse debut over 1m at Cork last month, should have come on for that run. Dropped in trip to 7f should suit and could well be able to win this race.
Signs of inexperience on debut over 7f at Gowran on soft ground, doing good work late on having been slowly away. There’s improvement to come and no forlorn hope in this.

Shaped well over fences last time, paying for a big move into contention when fading late on. That was a handicap. Drops down into a beginners chase here, which is there for the taking as she has plenty of experience over the bigger obstacles.

Coffeys Forge won a point a year ago at the 7th attempt after being placed in his previous three points. He joined Gordon Elliott in January and ran reasonably well in three handicap hurdles. Switching to fences for this beginners' chase should give him a chance of his first win under rules.

Not a strong race, and perhaps John O'Connell can get the best from Darkened, who he now trains as well as owns. The selection has some decent form in the book from his time with Noel Kelly, but there is just a suspicion he may be capable of better even at 9 years of age.

Ran well on debut last time in what will probably turn out to be a decent race. The winner is already thought good enough to be running in GP Company. Because the selection was a relatively cheap purchase, the terms of this race are in her favor as she receives plenty of weight. Something to bet on here.

Has had a couple of runs, the one at this track far better than his effort at Tipperary. But that experience should prove useful, and the extra furlong here is likely to suit. Worth a small each-way investment in a wide-open race.
Decent debut here over 5f and did not look @ home on Aw @ Dundalk on follow up run. Was only 4/1 & 9/1 for those races so dangerous to let them go off here @ current 40/1 in similar level maidens.

Not a strong event, and despite the lack of a recent run, Gavin Cromwell's new recruit, Arcland, should be good enough to make a winning start for his new trainer with conditions to suit and off a distinctly plausible mark.

Roaring Potter has been off for 1076 days with a back problem, wind op and contractual issues. Everything is tickety-boo now, and he is as fit as they can get him without racing. Trainer Keith Watson has found a good race for his comeback run. The track, trip, ground, and handicap mark all tick the boxes. The two question marks are: has he retained the ability he had, as some horses he has raced against are rated 130+? The other one is his attitude. He can be a bit stubborn sometimes, so Keith left a shotgun at his stable door last night just as an incentive :)

The model I run suggests the value bet here is Wrecking Ball Paul. This result has been driven by Wrecking Ball Paul having the highest RPR of this 10-runner race. He is not really penalized for it in the weights thanks to a kind official ranking. Looks to take advantage of this here and get over the line first in this 2m2f round trip. The model has indicated a 'low' reading here, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Looks well treated to my eye. Was running her best race at Thurles the time before last, right there competing until making an error at the hurdle and unable to recover. Dropped a pound for that and then tried in a tongue tie, which did no good. So now, with that removed and a much more experienced jockey in the plate, Me Philip Enright, off bottom weight, she can go close at huge odds.

Chiefs Kingdom has been placed several times over hurdles and last year switched to fences for two beginners chases in which he ran reasonably well in 4th and 5th. He ran 2nd in a maiden point in March only losing by three quarters of a length after leading and should have a good chance in this maiden hunters chase.

The model I run suggests Squire Ohara should win this one. Squire Ohara has the highest RPR of the runners here. All horses go out carrying the same initial weight. Claiming jockey on board claims 7 lbs, similar to a lot of the other runners, but importantly not at a disadvantage. Great form figures of 2321-2 and should go close again here today.

Highly promising Dark Angel gelding who was rapidly improving throughout last season as a 3yo ending his 3yo campaign with a hat trick of wins defying a penalty in process of completing that hat trick was last seen at Naas 26 days ago where finishing a promising well clear of rest 2nd/7 that was his seasonal reappearance run after a 198 day break and is entitled to strip fitter and be lot sharper at the finish this time out and looks set for another good season steps back up in trip to the 6 furlong trip and G M Lyons's inmate will highly appreciate this extra furlong jockey C T Keane takes the ride that being a positive booking and he has steered My Mate Alfie on those hat hat trick of wins and knows this Dark Angel gelding very well merits serious consideration and shouldn't have a big part to play in this Weatherbys Ireland Greenlands Group 2 Stakes over on the business end

The Irish 2000 Guineas looks to be between the two Juddmonte-owned, English-trained horses. It could go to the less exposed, unbeaten Cosmic Year, especially as Field Of Gold is drawn on the outside and may have to fight his way from the rear of the field again. He may have trouble in running at the Curragh.

Jessie Harrington's charge is the sole Group 1 winner in the field, last year's Futurity Stakes at Doncaster, and as such must look good each way value against the favourite. Indeed, on a line through Wimbledon Hawkeye, he has the beating of the Gosden runner. Described by his trainer as 'feisty' and 'loving a battle,' I think whatever beats him will know he's been in a race.

No doubt Field Of Gold should have won the Guineas when asked for his effort far too late, and he might copy Rosalion in making amends here. But I do think that Officer looks a really good prospect. With FOG having disappointed on his only visit overseas (soft ground also a potential excuse), I'm siding with the O'Brien colt. Raced just once as a juvenile, winning more cosily than the distance suggests, and was pitched into deep company on his first start this year, finishing 3rd in open company behind a race-fit Big Gossey, who is a solid enough yardstick, and Camille Pisarro, who was a Group 1 winner himself as a juvenile and placed 3rd in the French Guineas last time. That on just Officer's 2nd career start was impressive, and he got back to winning ways over C&D in a maiden last time. Hugely unexposed, and I have backed him already for the St James' Palace, where he's a huge 33/1 to take the Paddington route to Royal Ascot success.
